correctness.rationale: Complete exact graph proof: the first two matchings form paths because alternating steps translate left indices by nonzero \(b-1\). Below the threshold, later diagonal sums satisfy \(a_{j+1}>2a_j\) and each new matching edge has at most one old endpoint, preventing cycles. At and above the threshold, distinct left vertices \(L_{i(b-1)}\) and right vertices with indices \(c+1-i(b-1)\) and \(c+b\) form a simple \(2(b+1)\)-cycle; endpoint nonnegativity is exactly \(c\ge b(b-2)\). Every finite cycle uses finitely many levels. Finite exact-integer diagnostics (336) corroborate boundaries but do not prove the infinite statement; forest-to-complexity conversion uses the published theorem E.

value.rationale: The theorem completes a natural two-integer family of lacunary characteristic words at the level of exact extreme Abelian pattern complexity. The quadratic translation cutoff \(b(b-2)\) is sharp on both sides; the failure is witnessed by a uniform finite \(2(b+1)\)-cycle on just three incidence diagonals. The \(b=2\) versus \(b\ge3\) contrast and surviving \((b,c)=(3,2)\) example make this a substantive threshold rather than a direct substitution into an earlier growth criterion.
